modules.title: Project Dashboard
modules.limits: Projects are kept in this browser only. Create from a template or a specification file, open, rename, duplicate and delete, with status cards for the open project, and export or import a project bundle (specification, Studio data and asset files in one ZIP). Nothing is synced between browsers or devices, and a generation-plan state is not shown.

modules.title: Game Designer
modules.limits: The canonical v4 spec editors. With derivation off (the default) every field is owned by the Designer; while Level Studio or Gameplay derivation is on, the fields that module owns are read-only here.

modules.title: Asset Studio
modules.limits: Import, library, provenance, preview, delete protection and assignment of an asset to a kind. Library assets are exported in the Studio pack but do not reach the native apps; native sprites come only from the spec's own embedded atlas (spec v5), which the Sprite editor builds from a library image (see sprite-authoring).

modules.title: Sprite and Animation Editor
modules.limits: Sheet slicing, frame editing, animation sequences and a tick-based preview player, all inside Studio. The Atlas section builds the project's one native atlas from a sheet, assigns frames and ticks per frame to kinds, previews them and writes game.atlas and kinds[].sprite through the engine check (spec v5). One atlas per project; a sheet becomes the atlas only when its frames have one size.

modules.title: Level Studio
modules.limits: Only the active level compiles into the native spec, through an explicit Apply. Other levels are Studio-only variants exported as standalone specs and are not selectable inside the generated app. No wave end, per-level win rule or in-app level selection (see multi-level-in-app).

modules.title: Gameplay Systems
modules.limits: Forms for lives, win score, collectibles and enemies, with a reviewed Apply. Derivation is off by default; while on, Game Designer shows lives, win score and collisions read-only. Health, power-ups and progression need contract changes and stay planned.

modules.title: Backend and Services
modules.limits: Scaffold only: Firebase service choices, a read-only preview and Kotlin and Swift interfaces with inert stubs written once into extensions/ of the exported project, where the generated Android and iOS projects compile them. Not connected to any backend, no SDK, no keys or config files.

modules.title: Monetization
modules.limits: Mock and test placements with a labelled mock behaviour preview. The exported app compiles a labelled MOCK rewarded overlay from extensions/. No ad is requested, no ad network is contacted, no production ad ids and no ad unit id fields.

modules.title: Kiro Development
modules.limits: The static Developer Integration inventory with handoff prompts, Kiro templates and the Studio pack export with its ownership manifest and drift check, a drift view for a re-imported export and a proposal inbox. There is no Kiro connection and no in-browser AI call.

modules.title: Preview and Device Lab
modules.limits: Browser preview, determinism badge, hash-bound native evidence and an environments table that folds committed records for the exact spec hash. Studio runs no emulator, simulator or device. The simulator evidence covers build, install, launch and the first runtime ticks only, not gameplay, input or performance, and no physical-device record exists.

modules.title: Build and Release
modules.limits: The native source ZIP together with the Studio pack, a completeness check that blocks export on errors and a readiness checklist that proves only generated source for the current spec hash. Studio compiles nothing. No signing, upload or store-ready claim.

capabilities.title: Project list, status cards and bundle in and out
capabilities.limits: Studio-only and local to this browser. Stored projects other than the open one show the facts of their saved text; the engine checks them again when opened. A duplicate keeps the original project id because the specification is copied unchanged. The bundle ZIP is read by a hardened reader and a bundle that fails any check is refused and changes nothing; it carries Studio data and asset files, not a build. Not synced between browsers.

capabilities.title: Project Brain editors for the v4 spec with engine validation
capabilities.limits: Edits the canonical spec directly. Forms follow spec/schema.

capabilities.title: Canonical spec view, import and export through the engine serializer
capabilities.limits: One draft only; refused files leave the draft unchanged.

capabilities.title: Read-only fields owned by a derived module
capabilities.limits: Locks apply only while a derivation switch is on, and only to the spec pointers that module owns (the ownership tables are unit-tested). Locking in the rendered editors is checked by unit tests of the ownership rule, not by a recorded browser acceptance run.

capabilities.title: Lives, win score, collectibles and enemies compiled into lives, winScore and collisions
capabilities.limits: Opt-in derivation, default off. Review shows the diff and the engine verdict; nothing changes until Apply, as one undo step. The browser flow (lives, win score, collisions) runs in the foundry-flow script in CI. Health, power-ups and progression are not part of it.
capabilities.designRow: Lives, win score, collectible and enemy collision rows

capabilities.title: Difficulty ramp as later-starting spawners
capabilities.limits: Each step compiles to an extra spawner that starts later, together with its level through the explicit Apply. v4 spawners cannot stop or change, so the original wave keeps running. Steps are not a smooth ramp.

capabilities.title: Health, power-ups, progression
capabilities.limits: Designed only. Not buildable on the v4 contract.
capabilities.requires: A timed-state and persistence contract in the engine, which is outside this milestone.

capabilities.title: Active level compiled into initial entities and spawners
capabilities.limits: Active level only. Applied through an explicit action that the engine and a bounded oracle run must accept; one undo step. Difficulty steps compile as later-starting spawners.
capabilities.designRow: Initial placements, spawners, difficulty ramp (as later-starting spawners)

capabilities.title: Other levels exported as standalone spec variants
capabilities.limits: Variants are not selectable inside the generated app. Level Studio exports a ZIP that holds only studio-pack/derived/levels/<id>/monstera.spec.json, each checked by the engine. The Build and Release export does not add them.

capabilities.title: Level selection, per-level win rule and wave end inside the native app
capabilities.limits: Schema v4 has one runtime and spawners that never stop. Engine track E3, outside hackathon scope.
capabilities.requires: Engine and schema change after G6 closure.

capabilities.title: Import, library, provenance and assignment to kinds of images and audio
capabilities.limits: Studio-only: the native apps do not render or play assets, and an assignment is a link in the Studio data, not a spec field. Origin and license are user declarations; only the license shape is checked. MP3 trailing data cannot be detected by content checks; OGG and MP3 need a browser that can read their metadata.

capabilities.title: Assets rendered or played inside the generated apps
capabilities.limits: Assets imported into the Studio library do not reach the apps, and no audio is played. Native images come only from the spec's embedded atlas (see sprite-native-rendering).
capabilities.requires: An audio contract for sound. Library images reach the apps only through the native atlas (see sprite-authoring).

capabilities.title: Atlas slicing, frames and animation sequences with a tick-based preview
capabilities.limits: Studio preview and export only: the animation data travels in the Studio pack as studio data and no generated app reads it.

capabilities.title: Author the native sprite atlas and kind sprites in Studio
capabilities.limits: SIMULATOR-TESTED: a sheet authored in Studio was exported, generated and drawn on an Android emulator and an iOS simulator (frame log checked). Attract mode only, no gameplay or device. One atlas, equal-size frames up to 128x128, 24 KiB base64, two animated kinds, loops only.

capabilities.title: Sprite sheets and animations rendered inside the generated apps
capabilities.limits: Spec v5: one embedded PNG atlas per project, kind sprites of 0 to 4 frames, at most two animated kinds, frames chosen from the simulation tick. Built, launched and drawn on an Android emulator and an iOS simulator for both official games; gameplay and physical devices are not tested. Authoring is covered by sprite-authoring.

capabilities.title: Firebase and AdMob scaffold text and setup instructions
capabilities.limits: Not connected to any backend. The scaffold is written once into extensions/ (developer-owned, never overwritten on re-export) and compiled by the generated Gradle and SwiftPM projects. No SDK, keys or config files are produced. Compile and test results per platform are recorded in the E2 pull request and CI, not in this registry.
capabilities.designRow: Firebase interfaces and stubs, AdMob placements and mock rewarded ad

capabilities.title: Live Firebase connection, account or resource creation from Studio
capabilities.limits: Studio is static: no backend, no credentials, no network call to third parties.
capabilities.requires: A server and a credential model, which are not part of Studio.

capabilities.title: Placement configuration, frequency rules and a labelled mock rewarded ad
capabilities.limits: Mock and test placements only. The exported app shows a labelled MOCK overlay in place of an ad: no ad is requested, no ad network is contacted and there are no production ad ids.

capabilities.title: Production AdMob ids in Studio
capabilities.limits: Decision D7: Studio never stores or emits real ad ids; the developer adds them after export, in developer-owned files.

capabilities.title: Static inventory of agents, hooks, steering and MCP tools, plus handoff prompts
capabilities.limits: A static inventory stamped with the commit. It does not connect to Kiro.

capabilities.title: Studio pack export with ownership manifest and drift-check script
capabilities.limits: Scaffold files are regenerated only when unedited, write-once and extension files are never overwritten, and drift is reported, not repaired. Nothing in the pack is compiled into the app. The tools/check-drift.sh script needs bash; the Drift view in Studio does not.

capabilities.title: Review and apply an externally produced proposal
capabilities.limits: Reads one JSON file, checks it with the engine or the manifest rules, shows the difference and applies it only on acceptance. Who wrote a proposal is not verified.

capabilities.title: Direct AI provider calls from the browser
capabilities.limits: Decision D6: no provider calls and no keys in the browser during this milestone.
capabilities.requires: A server that holds keys; not part of Studio.

capabilities.title: Secure replaceable AI provider architecture
capabilities.limits: Roadmap only. Interface sketched in design section 8.3; no implementation.
capabilities.requires: A server that holds keys and a provider interface.

capabilities.title: Interactive preview driven by the unmodified engine
capabilities.limits: Browser environment. The preview drawing code mirrors the presentation modules for display only.

capabilities.title: Oracle against the recorded golden scenarios for the exact spec
capabilities.limits: Oracle environment inside the browser worker; says nothing about devices.

capabilities.title: Committed native build and simulator evidence bound to the exact spec SHA-256
capabilities.limits: Shows committed evidence only; an edited spec shows no evidence. The recorded simulator and emulator results cover build, install, launch and the first runtime ticks, not gameplay, input, performance or any physical device.

capabilities.title: Table of checks by environment (browser, oracle, jvm, swift-test, simulator, device)
capabilities.limits: Each row is folded from a committed record bound to the exact spec hash, so an edited spec reads no evidence. The device row never has a source and always reads no evidence. Covered by unit tests; no recorded browser acceptance run of this table.

capabilities.title: Running tests on emulators, simulators or physical devices from Studio
capabilities.limits: Studio is static and runs no device. Device Lab (G5) scripts produce evidence outside Studio.

capabilities.title: Native source ZIP generated by the engine in the browser
capabilities.limits: Source only. Nothing is compiled by Studio.

capabilities.title: Completeness check and release-readiness checklist
capabilities.limits: Errors block export and the generated files are checked against the engine plan; the export includes the Studio pack. The checklist proves only "generated" for the current spec hash; compiled, simulator and device results are not proven by Studio. It never claims store readiness.

capabilities.title: Signing, store upload or a store-ready claim
capabilities.limits: Out of scope: no signing, no upload, no store-ready claim without evidence.

capabilities.title: Project identity, module list and derivation switches (project manifest)
capabilities.limits: Stored and validated with every project, and its derivation switches drive Level Studio and Gameplay Systems. The module list is stored but does not decide which modules are shown.
capabilities.designRow: Project identity, module list, derivation switches

capabilities.title: Versioned sidecar manifest schemas with strict TypeScript validation
capabilities.limits: Validates Studio-owned manifests only. The engine validates the spec. Cross-manifest references are checked by the separate cross-reference index.

capabilities.title: Bundle, source-map, source, field and pack-import scan for credential-shaped strings
capabilities.limits: Pattern based, so it can miss an unusual secret; findings never print values. It reduces accidental leaks and is not a guarantee.

capabilities.title: nosniff and a Content-Security-Policy, report-only first
capabilities.limits: Verified on a local preview of the built site only. Not deployed: the Vercel Root Directory is confirmed (the repository root, 2026-11-16), but the live site sends neither header until the owner makes a report-only deployment and reviews its violations. Enforcement on production is not approved.
